mainTopic: A קבלן testifying for the borrower, and who can or cannot hold a חזקה: craftsmen, sharecroppers, robbers and their descendants, separated sons and divorced women
overview: The גמרא first finishes its talk about guarantors testifying. There are two opinions about whether a קבלן may testify for the borrower: one says he is like a regular ערב, and the other says he gains when the borrower keeps more land. Next, רבי יוחנן teaches that an אומן and an אריס cannot hold a חזקה, but their sons can. A גזלן and his son cannot, but his grandson can. The גמרא explains that the case is where witnesses saw the owner admit to the father. That admission helps the craftsman's and sharecropper's sons, but not the robber's son, because people admit things to a robber out of fear, as רב כהנא said. רבא adds that even the grandson loses if he claims through his robber grandfather. רבי יוחנן and רב חסדא then disagree about who counts as a גזלן. Finally, a ברייתא teaches that an אומן or אריס who leaves his job, a son who separated, and a divorced woman can hold a חזקה like anyone else. The גמרא asks why the divorced woman needed mentioning, and its answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Can an unconditional guarantor testify for the borrower?
steps.stepSummary: There are two opinions about whether a קבלן may testify for the borrower.
steps.simpleTranslation: A קבלן: some say he may testify, and some say he may not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא just said that a regular ערב may testify for the borrower about a field when the borrower owns other land. Now it asks the same question about a קבלן and brings two opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קבלן is a stronger guarantor, because the lender may collect from him directly even if the borrower can pay. So it is less clear whether he has a personal interest in the borrower keeping the field. One opinion says he may testify, and the other says he may not.

keyTerms.meaning: An unconditional guarantor. The lender can collect from him directly.

phrases.english: An unconditional guarantor —
phrases.notes: This is a guarantor the lender can go straight to, even if the borrower is able to pay.

phrases.english: some say he may testify,
and some say he may not testify.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי לַהּ מֵעִיד, וְאָמְרִי לַהּ אֵינוֹ מֵעִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the earlier rule about a regular ערב to the case of a קבלן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a dispute over whether a קבלן may testify for the borrower.

steps.title: The reasoning behind each opinion
steps.stepSummary: One side treats the קבלן like a regular ערב. The other side says he wants the borrower to keep both fields so that the lender collects from the borrower and not from him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The view that he may testify holds that he is like a regular guarantor. The view that he may not testify holds that he prefers both fields to stay with the borrower. That way, when the lender comes, he can take whatever he wants from the borrower.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reason behind each of the two opinions from Step 1.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lenient view says a קבלן is like a ערב: as long as the borrower has other land, the קבלן gains nothing from his testimony. The strict view says that even though the lender may go straight to the קבלן, the קבלן wants the borrower to have as much land as possible. Then the lender will likely collect from the borrower instead of from him. So he has a personal interest, and his testimony is not accepted.

keyTerms.meaning: It is better for him / he prefers

phrases.english: Those who say he may testify:
he is like a regular guarantor.
And those who say he may not testify:
because he prefers that both fields be in the borrower's hands,
so that when the creditor comes,
he will take whatever he wants.
phrases.notes: The idea is that the lender will be happy to collect from the borrower's land and leave the guarantor alone.

steps.whatToRemember: A witness who gains something from his testimony cannot testify. The question is whether a קבלן really gains anything when the borrower has other land.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasons for the two opinions listed in Step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Lenient view: a קבלן is like a ערב. Strict view: he has a personal interest because he wants the lender to collect from the borrower.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: who can hold a presumption of ownership
steps.stepSummary: An אומן and an אריס cannot hold a חזקה, but their sons can. A גזלן and his son cannot, but the robber's grandson can.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: A craftsman has no חזקה, but a craftsman's son does. A sharecropper has no חזקה, but a sharecropper's son does. A robber and a robber's son have no חזקה, but a robber's grandson does.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with רבי יוחנן's rule about which people can use a חזקה to prove ownership.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אומן and an אריס cannot use a חזקה, because their job explains why another person's property is in their hands. רבי יוחנן adds that their sons can use a חזקה. For a גזלן, the problem lasts one generation longer, until the grandson.

keyTerms.meaning: A presumption of ownership based on holding or using property
A craftsman who receives items to work on
A sharecropper who works someone else's field for a share of the crop

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
A craftsman cannot establish a presumption of ownership,
a craftsman's son can establish a presumption of ownership.
A sharecropper cannot establish a presumption of ownership,
a sharecropper's son can establish a presumption of ownership.

phrases.aramaic: גַּזְלָן וּבֶן גַּזְלָן אֵין לָהֶן חֲזָקָה,
phrases.english: A robber and a robber's son cannot establish a presumption of ownership,

phrases.aramaic: בֶּן בְּנוֹ שֶׁל גַּזְלָן יֵשׁ לוֹ חֲזָקָה.
phrases.english: a robber's grandson can establish a presumption of ownership.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אוּמָּן אֵין לוֹ חֲזָקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new topic, unrelated to the guarantor discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The sons of an אומן and an אריס can hold a חזקה. For a גזלן, only the grandson can.

steps.title: What case could this possibly be?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's rule. If the sons rely on their father's claim, none of them should win. If they don't rely on it, even the robber's son should win.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If they come with their father's claim, then even these sons (of the craftsman and sharecropper) should not win. If they do not come with their father's claim, then even the robber's son should win!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what case רבי יוחנן means, and argues that no simple case fits his distinction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose the son says 'it belonged to my father.' Then he is no stronger than his father, so the craftsman's son should also lose. Suppose instead the son claims the property on his own. Then his father's status should not matter, so the robber's son should also win. Either way, the difference between the sons disappears.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What are the circumstances?
These (here, the sons of the craftsman and sharecropper)

phrases.english: What is the case?
If they come with their father's claim,
then even these should not have a presumption.
phrases.notes: "These" means the craftsman's son and the sharecropper's son. Their fathers had no חזקה, so a claim built on the father's should fail too.

phrases.english: If they do not come with their father's claim,
then even a robber's son should have one!

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a simple request for information. The question is a challenge that tries to show רבי יוחנן's distinction cannot work in either case.
steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָמֵי? אִי אָתוּ בְּטַעְנְתָא דַאֲבוּהוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's rule from Step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's distinction between the sons of the אומן and אריס and the son of the גזלן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A two-sided argument: whether or not the son relies on his father's claim, all the sons should get the same result.

steps.title: The case: witnesses saw the owner admit
steps.stepSummary: The case is where witnesses saw the original owner admit to the father that the property was his. That admission is trusted for the craftsman and the sharecropper, but not for the robber.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the rule is needed where witnesses say: 'In our presence he admitted to him.' About these sons, we can say they are telling the truth. About this one, even though the owner admitted, he is still not believed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by describing a specific case where the sons really are different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Witnesses testify that the original owner admitted to the father that the property belonged to him. That backs up the sons of the אומן and אריס, so their claim is accepted. With a גזלן, the admission proves nothing, so his son still cannot win.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for this case (introduces a narrow case)

phrases.english: No, it is needed
where witnesses say:
'In our presence he admitted to him.'
phrases.notes: The original owner admitted to the father that the property really was the father's.

phrases.english: These — one can say
they are telling the truth.
This one — even though he admitted,
he is still not believed,

steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the rule to a specific case (witnesses saw an admission)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without a specific case, the sons should all be treated the same.
steps.terutzMaskana: When the owner admitted, the admission counts for an אומן or אריס but not for a גזלן.

steps.title: רב כהנא: people admit to a robber out of fear
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא's saying explains why an admission to a גזלן means nothing: the owner admitted only because he was afraid.
steps.simpleTranslation: This follows רב כהנא, who said: If he had not admitted to him, the robber would have brought him and his donkey to the taskmaster.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רב כהנא's saying to support why an admission to a robber is not trusted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A robber is assumed to be a violent person. The owner may have said 'it's yours' only to avoid serious trouble, not because it was true. So his admission does not support the robber's son.

keyTerms.meaning: Taskmaster, a harsh officer (here, an expression for big trouble)

phrases.english: in line with Rav Kahana,
as Rav Kahana said:
If he had not admitted to him,
he would have brought him and his donkey to the taskmaster.
phrases.notes: This is an expression. It means the robber would have made terrible trouble for him if he refused.

steps.whatToRemember: An admission only counts if it was given freely. An admission to a גזלן is assumed to come from fear, so his son still cannot hold a חזקה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the key reason רבי יוחנן treats a robber's family more strictly than a craftsman's or sharecropper's family.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the claim in Step 5 that an admission to a גזלן is not trusted.
steps.raayaObject: That an admission to a גזלן does not prove ownership
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב כהנא's saying that people admit to a robber out of fear

steps.title: When even the robber's grandson cannot hold a חזקה
steps.stepSummary: רבא says that the גזלן's grandson also has no חזקה if he bases his claim on his grandfather's ownership.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא says: Sometimes even a robber's grandson has no חזקה. When? When he comes to court claiming the land through his father's father.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds a limit to the rule that a גזלן's grandson can hold a חזקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier we learned that a גזלן's grandson can win with a חזקה. רבא says this only works when the grandson has his own claim. If he says 'this belonged to my grandfather,' he is leaning on the robber's claim, and the robber's claim is worthless.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What are the circumstances?

phrases.english: Rava says:

phrases.aramaic: פְּעָמִים שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ בֶּן בְּנוֹ שֶׁל גַּזְלָן
phrases.english: There are times when even a robber's grandson
also does not have a chazaka.
phrases.notes: This limits רבי יוחנן's rule back in Step 3, that the robber's grandson can hold a חזקה.

phrases.english: What is the case?
For example, where he comes
with the claim of his father's father.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: פְּעָמִים שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ בֶּן בְּנוֹ שֶׁל גַּזְלָן נָמֵי אֵין לוֹ חֲזָקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Puts a limit on רבי יוחנן's rule about the robber's grandson
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גזלן's grandson who claims through his grandfather has no חזקה.

steps.title: Who counts as a robber?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what kind of person is called a גזלן for these rules.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case of a robber?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a definition of a גזלן. This sets up the two answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that a גזלן cannot hold a חזקה needs a clear definition. Is it someone known to have stolen this field, or anyone known to be violent?

keyTerms.meaning: A robber, someone who takes property by force

phrases.english: What is the case of a robber?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a definition of the גזלן mentioned in the rules above
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which person is treated as a גזלן who cannot hold a חזקה

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: known to have robbed this field
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says a גזלן is someone known to hold this very field by robbery.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says: For example, where it is known that he holds this field through robbery.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives the first definition of a גזלן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, it is not enough to be a violent person in general. It must be known that he took this specific field by force.

keyTerms.meaning: It was established, it became known

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan says:
For example, where it is established about this field
that he holds it through robbery.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: כְּגוֹן שֶׁהוּחְזַק עַל שָׂדֶה זוֹ בְּגַזְלָנוּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of who is a גזלן
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזלן is someone known to hold this specific field by robbery

steps.title: רב חסדא: a family known for killing over money
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says that even a member of a family known to kill people over money counts as a גזלן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב חסדא says: For example, the family of so-and-so, who kill people over money matters.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא gives a second, wider definition of a גזלן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב חסדא, it is enough to belong to a known violent family. People are too scared to protest against them, so their silence proves nothing about any field.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ties back to רב כהנא's idea in Step 6: when the owner is afraid, his silence or admission means nothing.

phrases.english: And Rav Chisda says:
For example, those of the family of so-and-so,
who kill people over money matters.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר: כְּגוֹן דְּבֵית פְּלוֹנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a wider definition than רבי יוחנן
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A member of a violent family known for killing over money is a גזלן

steps.title: A ברייתא: people who regain the ability to hold a חזקה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that an אומן or אריס who leaves his job can hold a חזקה, and that a בן שחלק and an אשה שנתגרשה are like everyone else.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: A craftsman has no חזקה; if he left his craft, he has a חזקה. A sharecropper has no חזקה; if he left his sharecropping, he has a חזקה. A son who separated and a woman who was divorced are like all other people.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא listing people who normally cannot hold a חזקה, and explains when they can.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The אומן and אריס lose their חזקה only because their job explains why they are holding the item. Once they leave the job, that explanation is gone. A son and a wife normally use family property freely, but once they separate or divorce, they are treated like strangers.

keyTerms.meaning: A son who separated from his father's money

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
A craftsman has no chazaka;
if he left his craft, he has a chazaka.
A sharecropper has no chazaka;
if he left his sharecropping, he has a chazaka.
A son who separated, and a woman who was divorced:
they are like all other people.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אוּמָּן אֵין לוֹ חֲזָקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא with more rules about who can hold a חזקה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אומן or אריס who left his job, a בן שחלק, and an אשה שנתגרשה can hold a חזקה like anyone else.

steps.title: Why mention the divorced woman? It is obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees that the separated son needed to be taught, but asks why the ברייתא needed to mention the divorced woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that the son who separated needed to be taught, because you might have thought the father just let him use it. The ברייתא teaches that this is not so. But a divorced woman? That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא for teaching something that seems obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the son, you might think a father would let his son use the land for free even after they separated, so the father's silence proves nothing. The ברייתא needed to say no. But a divorced woman has no tie to her ex-husband, so why say she is like everyone else?

keyTerms.meaning: He fully let it go, he forgave it

phrases.english: Granted, the son who separated needed to be taught,
since you might have thought:
he let it go for him,
phrases.notes: The father simply let his son use the land, so the father's silence would prove nothing.

phrases.english: so it teaches us that this is not so.
But a woman who was divorced:
that is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges why the ברייתא included one of its cases
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's mention of the אשה שנתגרשה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A divorced woman has no connection to her ex-husband's property, so saying she can hold a חזקה adds nothing new.

steps.title: The answer begins: it is needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts to answer that the divorced woman's case is needed in a special situation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer. This line sets up a special case that is explained at the start of the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'לא צריכא' tells us the ברייתא is not saying something obvious. It is pointing to a specific situation where the divorced woman's law is not simple.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for a specific case

phrases.english: No, it is needed...
phrases.notes: The answer continues on the next amud, where the גמרא describes the special case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the challenge about the divorced woman
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case to a special situation (לא צריכא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The divorced woman's case seems obvious and unnecessary
steps.terutzMaskana: It is needed for a special situation, which the גמרא goes on to explain
